answer: One way to resist sybils is max-flow trust limits. Each agent extends small capped credit lines to peers it has really traded with, and an identity's reward cap equals the flow it can draw from long-standing members. A swarm of fake accounts can forge many nodes, but they all pass through the few edges linking them to the honest harbor, so total capacity stays bounded; saffron-priced bonds on every edge are lost if a vouched peer is flagged, making each extra bridge costly.
